card.reference: The original textkit sources at the commit (several thousand lines, deleted from the image). It scores 1.

spike.commands_log: git fetch/checkout e7b14db1 in /p/src; yarn build; vitest run packages/textkit packages/layout (x3, 1310/1310 pass each); tests/oracle.test.ts generates 20 layouts (x2, byte-identical); bestFit-only variant compared against the oracle; find for textkit copies outside the workspace symlink and in the yarn cache (none found).
spike.headroom_note: A greedy best-fit-only proxy scored a mean of 0.40 against the oracle, per layout 0.00 to 1.00, so there is a partial-credit curve. Knuth-Plass, justification and hyphenation fidelity leave room above it.
spike.notes: Not run: the stubbed-base check (the textkit tests import src directly, so stubs would fail them), an offline build with the network off, and the .git scrub. The oracle generator used the reference in the repo, so the 20/20 reference pass is by construction. The 20 layouts used the one Latin font with pseudo-random widths, alignments, ellipsis, maxLines and hyphenation factor. The orphans option was not exercised. The greedy proxy was best-fit only, not a hand-written greedy wrap. Image size is an estimate, with node_modules at 634 MB. The 20 stable base failures from the probe are all in the renderer package, outside textkit and layout.

facts.claim: react-pdf repo has a packages/ tree at commit e7b14db1 that includes a packages/textkit directory (and layout, font, hyphenate)
packages/textkit at that commit is @react-pdf/textkit v7.0.1, licence MIT, repository diegomura/react-pdf directory packages/textkit
textkit's dependencies are @react-pdf/fns, @react-pdf/hyphenate, bidi-js, unicode-properties (so hyphenate is a separate package that the rebuild can keep)

packages/textkit/tests contains one visible top-level test file (index.test.ts) and 12 subdirectories (attributedString, engines, glyph, glyph-indices, internal, layout, rect, run, shape, string-indices, utils, assets); total test count not visible
textkit's source modules (bidi, linebreaker, justification, fontSubstitution, scriptItemizer, wordHyphenation, textDecoration, layoutEngine, fromFragments) are listed in the README
@react-pdf/textkit is a fork of foliojs/textkit by devongovett, so a second public upstream copy exists
npm package page for @react-pdf/textkit (latest version, licence, publish date)
Linebreaker is Knuth-Plass with a best-fit fallback, with tolerance retries (+5 up to 50) and hyphen penalties 600 ragged / 100 justified
foliojs/textkit upstream repository exists and is MIT-licensed
Total line count of the textkit sources ('several thousand lines')

full_card.band: Tier 8 h. No dated public evidence of agent results on this task, so Band capped at 3. A frontier agent may reach partial credit on wrap, alignment and truncation; exact numeric justification and orphan behaviour is the hard part and the weaker model should stop at basic left-aligned wrap.
full_card.build_cost: About 3-4 days: stub-and-scrub the snapshot, generate ~500 oracle layouts from the reference, check the grader ignores base failures, validate hidden cases against a second valid implementation
full_card.deliverable: Rebuilt textkit: line breaking (Knuth-Plass style with fallback), justification, hyphenation, run attribution, ellipsis/truncation, bidi runs, text-block layout, behind existing public APIs; PDF output works again
full_card.gates_anticheat: Strip .git and any past commits; scrub node_modules, yarn/npm cache and layout dist of textkit; hidden oracle outputs and generator outside image; hidden layouts fixed at grading; grader ignores the 22 tests that fail at the unmodified commit
full_card.grading_surface: vitest suites of textkit and layout (base fails all graded cases) plus about 500 hidden generated layouts compared numerically (fragment and line boxes) against the original; proportional credit. Oracle generated by running the reference offline.
full_card.local_fit: Node + vitest, CPU only; smoke build 76 s, suite 44 s, deterministic; fits 8 cores / 16 GB
full_card.lookup: direct: complete MIT implementation public on npm and GitHub with full history; not installable offline and not in image; recallable only in outline
full_card.provenance: diegomura/react-pdf @ e7b14db1 (MIT); packages/textkit = @react-pdf/textkit 7.0.1; forked from foliojs/textkit; full git history public on GitHub; @react-pdf/textkit also on npm
full_card.reference: Original textkit sources at e7b14db1 (MIT, TypeScript), deleted from image; scores 1 by definition. Line count not verified.
full_card.ships: Pinned Node/TypeScript monorepo snapshot at base with textkit src stubbed; layout, font, hyphenate, render kept; must be history-less and free of any textkit copy in node_modules, yarn/npm caches, or dist
full_card.similarity: Max l0 neighbour 0.237 (S-im-012), then 0.215 (S-im-006), 0.205 (S-im-008); css_layout_engine 0.146; none is a public task with the same subject, so no K1

Band.why: No dated public evidence of frontier agent results on this task; capped at 3. Exact justification and orphan fidelity is hard, so a frontier agent averages well below reference.

Build.why: Estimated 3-4 days: scrub snapshot, generate ~500 oracle layouts, validate grader against a second implementation.

Fit.why: Node/TypeScript, CPU only, smoke build and suite deterministic and under a minute each.

Hor.why: Several interacting modules (breaking, justification, hyphenation, bidi, truncation, layout) at 8 h tier.

Lic.why: MIT, confirmed in packages/textkit/package.json; shipping allowed.

Multi.why: Distinct levers (breaking, justification, hyphenation, ellipsis, bidi, run attribution) give natural partial-credit buckets.

Nov.why: Max neighbour 0.237 is a seed, not a public task; no CROWDED overlap; css_layout_engine 0.146 is below 0.15.

Real.why: Pinned MIT monorepo at e7b14db1 with packages/textkit confirmed; real release history and 16.8k stars from seed.

Ref.why: Complete MIT TypeScript implementation scoring exactly 1; upstream reference is in the original repo.

Seal.why: Reference is public on npm and GitHub with full history; sealable only with history-less snapshot and scrubbed node_modules and caches. Partial recall is possible but exact numeric output is not.

Surf.why: ~500 hidden numeric layouts plus vitest suites; not an unlimited generator, so 4 not 5.

spike_plan.kill_if: Oracle output is nondeterministic, or a textkit copy or .git survives in the snapshot and cannot be scrubbed, or the greedy wrap scores zero or full credit on all layouts (no partial-credit curve).
spike_plan.pass_if: Oracle generation is deterministic across two runs; the stubbed base fails all graded cases; the scrub finds no textkit copy or git history; a greedy wrap earns partial, non-zero credit.
steps: In a throwaway Linux container with network, clone diegomura/react-pdf at e7b14db1 and run the smoke build path (already green: build 76 s, suite 44 s).
Confirm textkit tests run: record the per-test results of packages/textkit and packages/layout, and note the 22 failing tests at the base commit.
Generate 20 oracle layouts from the reference textkit across text, fonts, widths, alignments, truncation and orphans; save fragment and line boxes as JSON.
Create a stubbed copy of packages/textkit that throws, and run layout tests; confirm the base fails the graded cases.
Re-run the oracle generator with a second run to confirm byte-identical output (determinism).
Check the snapshot scrub: search node_modules, yarn/npm cache and layout dist for any textkit copy and for .git; list any hits.
Write a minimal greedy wrap in place of breaking and score the 20 oracle layouts to confirm the tolerance comparison gives partial credit, not all-or-nothing.

v1.summary: The react-pdf textkit rebuild (MIT, pinned at e7b14db1, packages/textkit confirmed) is a real, licence-clean task with a strong reference and multi-lever partial credit, and it passes the gates with no kill. The main risk is sealing: the complete reference is public on npm and GitHub, so the snapshot must be history-less with all textkit copies scrubbed, and Band is capped at 3 without dated evidence.

v2.note: Real MIT package and the original source is a perfect reference. textkit's size is unverified and may be only a few thousand lines. Its tests are fine-grained per function: if shipped, the rebuild becomes a guided fill-in and a weaker model may keep up (K8 watch). Graded tests should be hidden, with only a sample shipped. The upstream source is public on npm and in foliojs/textkit, so scrub all caches. The 22 failing tests at the base commit must be excluded, and the fontkit glyph path must stay deterministic.
